question: How long does a new isolated read-only iCloud mount with an empty Cirrove metadata cache take to publish a complete root listing, and how long do first openings of a root folder and a nested folder take?
arms: new private account state with only the existing Cirrove-owned sealed iCloud session and short key, no metadata or content cache
first root listing and its item count
first listing of a root folder, then a nested folder of roughly 50 entries, then a second root folder
warm repeat of the same paths
endpoint: Record monotonic elapsed time, item counts and filesystem errors for each listing. A result is complete only when the directory iterator finishes; do not infer completeness from a partially rendered File Manager window. Compare with counts in the existing mount. Record no secrets, provider bodies, item IDs, file names, cursor URLs or signed URLs.
prediction: The root and each cold folder will wait for an Apple metadata request and may take seconds or tens of seconds; warm repeats will be much faster. The current on-demand design will not index the entire account when connecting.
scope: A new isolated Cirrove state and read-only mount; the existing iCloud validation mount, regular Cirrove service and other providers remain untouched. No cloud mutations.

results.metadata_cache_at_start: empty; only accounts.json and the encrypted session were copied

results.note: These later attempts establish eventual completeness, not exact time-to-completeness for these three paths.

interpretation: The first open of an unvisited folder returned an immediate empty listing or ENOENT; the same paths later contained their expected entries. This reproduces the owner's symptom. The root-only on-demand feed had already stored a completed cursor, and Store's unknown-directory fallback treats a completed feed as a complete tree. The first cached read therefore falsely reports empty, while the activity refresh fetches the folder asynchronously. Fix and retest before calling on-demand navigation reliable.
